en:block:am-draw-ladder.text: Now the draw ladder. This one's sixteen minutes. Straight shot again, with the cue ball eight inches from the object ball to start. Then sixteen inches, then two feet. If you have a cue ball with dots on it, use that one. At each distance, first try to draw the cue ball back about six inches. Then about a foot, and then farther. Keep your cue level and speed up smoothly through the ball. You don't need to hit harder. The goal is to pot the ball and pull the cue ball straight back, stopping where you meant it to.

en:block:am-follow-ladder.text: Time for the follow ladder. Twelve minutes. Same straight setup, with the cue ball one, two, then three feet from the object ball. Before every shot, decide how far you want the cue ball to roll on: six inches, a foot, or two feet. Then get it there with a smooth follow stroke, not just by hitting harder. You want the cue ball to roll straight through and stop close to the distance you picked.

en:block:am-precision-pocket.text: Last one this morning: the precision pocket drill. Ten minutes. Shoot long straight shots and slight cuts, switching between the left and right corner pockets. If you have a pocket reducer, you can use it here. Be strict with yourself. If a ball rattles in the jaws, count it as a miss, even if it drops. Aim for the center of the pocket every time, with a calm, steady stroke.

en:block:am-stop-ladder.text: Next up, the stop shot ladder. Twelve minutes. Set up a straight shot with the cue ball a foot from the object ball. Later you'll move it back to two feet, and then three. That's ten shots at each distance. Start by hitting the cue ball right in the center. When the distance changes, change your speed, not just where the tip hits. Hold your finish and watch what the cue ball does. A good stop is when it stays within about three inches of where it hit the object ball.

en:block:am-straight-warmup.text: Let's warm up with straight balls. You've got ten minutes. Put an object ball in line with a corner pocket, and start with the cue ball about a foot behind it. As you get comfortable, move the cue ball back to two feet, then three, then four. Shoot in sets of five, and take your time. Whenever you miss, stop and ask yourself why. Was it your aim, your stroke, or where you hit the cue ball? You're looking for the ball to drop right in the middle of the pocket, with the cue ball staying on the line.

en:block:pm-3ball.text: Now the three-ball pattern drill. Fifteen minutes. Throw out three balls in a layout you can run, and take ball in hand for the first shot. Before you shoot, say your plan out loud: which ball you'll play in what order, and where the cue ball should go each time. If you make a big position mistake, set the layout up again and start over. You're aiming to run all three without needing a rescue shot.

en:block:pm-5ball.text: Time for the five-ball clearance. Thirteen minutes. Spread five balls around the table with nothing blocking them, and start with ball in hand. Choose the easiest route, move the cue ball as little as you can, and skip side spin unless you really need it. When a run fails, make a note of why it ended. The goal is to clear all five without a miss and without losing position.

en:block:pm-cut-blocks.text: Let's start the afternoon with cut shots. You've got twelve minutes. Pick three cut angles you can set up the same way every time, roughly thirty, forty-five and sixty degrees. Practise each one cutting left and cutting right, six shots each. Keep the object ball and the pocket in the same place for each little set. Get the potting line right first. Once that feels solid, start paying attention to where the cue ball ends up. You want to make these consistently, both to the left and to the right.

en:block:pm-one-rail.text: Next, one-rail position. Fifteen minutes. Mark a small target area, about a foot to a foot and a half across, where you want the cue ball for your next shot. Pot the object ball and send the cue ball off one rail into that area. Change only one thing at a time: your speed, follow or draw, or a touch of side. And before each shot, picture the path the cue ball will take. It only counts if the cue ball lands in your target, not just somewhere you could still shoot from.

en:block:pm-review.text: Let's finish with a short review, about five minutes. Think back over today, and set up the two or three worst shots or decisions you had. Don't end the day just knocking balls around. Shoot that exact problem again and again until you understand what went wrong. You're done when you know what caused the miss, and what you'll change to fix it.

en:test:cut.text: Next, cut shots. Pick one medium cut angle and stick with it. Shoot ten cutting to the left, then ten cutting to the right. Don't change the angle after a miss.

en:test:draw.text: Next, the draw test. Straight shot, with the cue ball two feet from the object ball. Put the object ball close enough to the pocket that you'll make it every time. Shoot five, and measure how far the cue ball comes back on each one. Use the same cue ball every time you test.

en:test:fiveBall.text: Last test: five-ball clearance. If you can, use the same five-ball layout as last time, and start with ball in hand. You get five tries. Count how many times you clear the table, and for any run that fails, note the main reason.

en:test:stop.text: Now the stop shot test. Set up a straight shot with the cue ball two feet from the object ball. You get ten shots. A shot counts when the ball goes in and the cue ball stops within about three inches of where it made contact. Try to use the same speed every time.

en:test:straight.text: First test: the long straight pot. Place the object ball about a foot, or a foot and a half, from a corner pocket. Put the cue ball four feet behind it, in a perfectly straight line. You get ten shots. Use the same pocket and the same distances every time you take this test.

en:tips:am-draw-ladder.text: Here's what usually goes wrong with draw. People hit harder, when they should hit lower and cleaner. Keep the back of your cue down, so the cue stays level. And keep accelerating through the cue ball. Don't slow down at contact.

en:tips:am-follow-ladder.text: Watch out for a few things. Don't just push harder; control the distance with a smooth stroke. Pick your distance before you get down on the shot. And hit straight above center, so the cue ball doesn't drift off the line.

en:tips:am-precision-pocket.text: A couple of reminders. Be honest: a ball that rattles in the jaws is a miss. Aim for the very center of the pocket, not just somewhere in it. And if you notice you're speeding up, pause and go through your routine again.

en:tips:am-stop-ladder.text: Quick reminders. A real stop shot is hit at center, not with draw. When the distance gets longer, add a little speed rather than hitting lower. And stay down after the shot, so you can see exactly what the cue ball did.

en:tips:am-straight-warmup.text: A few things to watch. Keep your head still until the ball is in the pocket. Let the cue go straight through, and don't steer it at the end. And after a miss, take a breath and work out why before you set up again.

en:tips:cut.text: Keep the same angle all the way through, even after a miss. Don't rush the side you find harder. And put the object ball back in exactly the same spot each time.

en:tips:draw.text: Measure each draw properly; don't just guess. Keep the same stroke for all five, and don't start hitting harder. And put the object ball close enough to the pocket that you never miss it.

en:tips:fiveBall.text: Use the same layout if you can, so the results mean something. Take your time on the first shot; it sets up the whole run. And when a run fails, notice why it ended.

en:tips:pm-3ball.text: A few reminders. Plan all three shots before you hit the first one. You don't need perfect position, just a good angle for the next shot. And if the position goes badly wrong, set the layout up again instead of trying to rescue it.

en:tips:pm-5ball.text: Here's what usually ends a run. Picking a route that's harder than it needs to be. Sending the cue ball a long way when a short move would do. And using side spin when you don't need it. Keep it simple.

en:tips:pm-cut-blocks.text: Common mistakes on cuts. Changing the angle and the speed at the same time, so you can't tell what went wrong. Missing the same way again and again, always too thin or always too thick. Notice which way you miss, and adjust. And thinking about the cue ball too early, before the pot itself feels solid.

en:tips:pm-one-rail.text: Be strict here. If the cue ball isn't in the target area, it doesn't count, even if you still have a shot. Change just one thing at a time, so you learn what each change does. And always picture the cue ball's path before you shoot.

en:tips:pm-review.text: For the review, don't just knock balls around. Pick the shots that really cost you, set them up exactly, and don't move on until you can say what caused the miss and what you'll do differently.

en:tips:stop.text: Hit center ball for a true stop. Don't use draw to fake it. Use the same speed on every shot. And be honest: if the cue ball rolls more than about three inches, it's not a success.

en:tips:straight.text: For this test, keep the setup exactly the same every time, so your scores can be compared. Take your time on every shot, including the last few. And on a long shot, stay down until the ball drops.

zh:block:am-draw-ladder.text: 现在练低杆，这个环节十六分钟。还是直线球，主球离目标球先放二十厘米，差不多一个手掌，然后四十、六十厘米。有带点的训练主球的话，就用它。每个距离，先试着把主球拉回十五厘米左右，就是拇指和食指张开那么长；再拉回三十厘米；然后再远一点。球杆尽量放平，出杆平顺地加速，不用使蛮劲。目标是球打进，主球沿着原来的线拉回来，停在你想要的位置。

zh:block:am-follow-ladder.text: 下面练高杆，十二分钟。还是直线球，主球离目标球三十、六十、九十厘米。每打一杆之前，先想好要让主球往前跟多远：十五厘米、三十厘米，还是六十厘米。然后用顺滑的高杆把它送过去，不是靠打得更重。主球要顺着线往前走，停在你定好的距离附近。

zh:block:am-precision-pocket.text: 上午最后一项，精准进袋，十分钟。打长直线球和小角度的切球，左右两个底袋轮流打。手边有缩袋器的话，这个环节可以用上。对自己严格一点：球在袋口晃了一下、磕了袋角，就算最后掉进去了，也记作没进。每一杆都瞄袋口正中间，动作保持稳定。

zh:block:am-stop-ladder.text: 接下来练定杆，一共十二分钟。摆一个直线球，主球离目标球三十厘米，之后再拉到六十、九十厘米，每个距离打十杆。先用中杆。距离变了，主要靠调整力度，不要光改击球点。打完保持收杆姿势，看着主球。主球停在撞击点附近，大约四根手指并拢那么宽的范围以内，就算打好了。

zh:block:am-straight-warmup.text: 我们先用直线球热身，一共十分钟。把目标球和底袋摆成一条直线，主球先放在目标球后面大约三十厘米，差不多一个半手掌。打顺了以后，再把主球往后挪，六十、九十，最后到一百二十厘米。每五杆一组，别着急。每次没进，先停下来想一想：是瞄准的问题、出杆的问题，还是击球点的问题？目标是球从袋口正中间进去，主球也基本留在原来的线上。

zh:block:pm-3ball.text: 现在练三球线路，十五分钟。随手摆三颗能打的球，第一杆自由球。出杆之前，先把计划说出来：先打哪颗，后打哪颗，每一杆主球要停在哪儿。如果走位出了大问题，就把球按原样再摆一遍，从头再来。目标是三颗球一口气打完，中间不用补救。

zh:block:pm-5ball.text: 下面是五球清台，十三分钟。把五颗球随意散开，别互相挡住，开局自由球。选最简单的线路，主球能少走就少走，没必要的话就别加塞。没清完的时候，记一下是因为什么断的。目标是五颗球全部清完，不失误，走位也不失控。

zh:block:pm-cut-blocks.text: 下午我们从切球开始，十二分钟。选三个你每次都能摆出来的角度，大概三十度、四十五度和六十度。向左切、向右切都要练，每种打六杆。每一小组里，目标球和袋口的位置都不要动。先把进球的线路找准，有把握了，再开始注意主球停在哪里。目标是不管向左还是向右，都能稳定地打进。

zh:block:pm-one-rail.text: 接下来练一库走位，十五分钟。先在台面上标出一个小目标区，大约三十到四十五厘米，也就是一个半到两个手掌那么大，作为下一杆主球要去的地方。打进目标球，让主球吃一库以后走进这个区域。每次只改变一样东西：力度、高低杆，或者一点点加塞。出杆前，先在脑子里把主球的路线走一遍。主球真正进了目标区才算数，不是停在一个还能打的地方就行。

zh:block:pm-review.text: 最后做个简短复盘，大概五分钟。回想一下今天打得最差的两三杆球，或者判断错的地方，把它们再摆出来。别用随便打打来收尾。就盯着那一杆反复打，直到想明白问题出在哪儿。知道了为什么没进，也知道要改什么，今天就算练好了。

zh:test:cut.text: 下一项，切球。选一个中等的切球角度，固定不变。向左切十杆，再向右切十杆。没进也不要改角度。

zh:test:draw.text: 下一项，低杆测试。直线球，主球离目标球六十厘米。目标球要离袋口近一点，保证每杆都能打进。打五杆，每一杆都量一下主球拉回了多远。每次测试都用同一颗主球。

zh:test:fiveBall.text: 最后一项：五球清台。可以的话，用和上次一样的五球球型，开局自由球。一共五次机会。数一数清台成功了几次；没清完的，记下主要原因。

zh:test:stop.text: 现在测定杆。摆一个直线球，主球离目标球六十厘米，差不多三个手掌。一共十杆。球进了，而且主球停在撞击点附近、大约四根手指并拢宽的范围内，才算成功。每次尽量用同样的力度。

zh:test:straight.text: 第一项测试：长直线球。目标球放在离底袋三十到四十五厘米的地方，主球放在目标球后面一百二十厘米，完全成一条直线。一共打十杆。每次测试都用同一个袋口、同样的距离。

zh:tips:am-draw-ladder.text: 低杆最常见的问题是：靠使劲，而不是打得更低、更干净。杆尾要压低，让球杆尽量放平。击球的时候要一直加速穿过主球，别在碰到球的时候收力。

zh:tips:am-follow-ladder.text: 注意几点。不要光靠推得更猛，要用顺滑的出杆控制距离。趴下之前，先想好让主球跟多远。击球点要在正中线的上方，不然主球会带塞跑偏。

zh:tips:am-precision-pocket.text: 提醒两三点。对自己诚实一点，在袋口晃进去的球算没进。要瞄袋口的正中间，而不是只要进袋就行。发现自己越打越快的时候，停一下，把击球前的准备动作再走一遍。

zh:tips:am-stop-ladder.text: 提醒几点。真正的定杆是打中杆，不是用低杆凑出来的。距离远了，要加一点力度，而不是把杆打得更低。打完先别起身，看清楚主球到底怎么走的。

zh:tips:am-straight-warmup.text: 注意这几点。球进袋之前，头不要动。出杆要直直地送出去，最后一刻别拐杆。没进的时候，先缓一口气，想明白原因再摆下一颗。

zh:tips:cut.text: 整个测试都用同一个角度，没进也别改。自己不擅长的那一边，别急着打。每次都把目标球放回完全相同的位置。

zh:tips:draw.text: 每一杆都认真量一下，别光用眼睛估。五杆用同样的出杆，别越打越用力。目标球要放得离袋口够近，保证不会打丢。

zh:tips:fiveBall.text: 能用同一个球型就用同一个，成绩才有意义。第一杆别急，它决定了整盘的走位。没清完的时候，留意一下是因为什么断的。

zh:tips:pm-3ball.text: 提醒几点。打第一杆之前，先把三杆都想好。走位不用完美，给下一杆留一个好角度就够了。如果走位出了大问题，就把球摆回去再来，不要硬救。

zh:tips:pm-5ball.text: 清台失败，常常是因为这几个原因：线路选得太难；主球本来走一小段就行，却让它跑了大半张台；还有没必要的时候加了塞。越简单越好。

zh:tips:pm-cut-blocks.text: 切球常见的错误有这几个。角度和力度一起改，结果不知道问题出在哪。总往同一边偏，老是切薄，或者老是切厚，要留意自己偏向哪边，然后调整。还有，进球还没打稳，就开始想主球停哪儿。

zh:tips:pm-one-rail.text: 这项要严格。主球没进目标区就不算，哪怕还有球可打。每次只改一样东西，这样才知道每个改变的效果。出杆前，一定先想好主球的路线。

zh:tips:pm-review.text: 复盘的时候，别随便打打。挑真正让你丢分的球，按原样摆好。没想明白为什么没进、下次怎么改之前，不要换下一个。

zh:tips:stop.text: 用中杆打真正的定杆，别用低杆去凑。每一杆用同样的力度。还有要诚实，主球滚出去超过四根手指宽，就不算成功。

zh:tips:straight.text: 这项测试，每次摆法要完全一样，成绩才有可比性。每一杆都别着急，最后几杆也一样。长台更要注意，球进之前头别抬。
